# std.system

<!-- Generated by `badger doc std` from the checked interfaces (badger 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand. -->

Lifecycle-managed systems.

`system { key: component(provider, config), ... }` is elaborated by the
compiler into typed nodes in dependency order (references are checked and
cycles rejected before anything runs) followed by `system.plan`.

## Types

```badger
pub extern type Brand<S>
```

Region brand of a running system (cannot escape `system.run`).

### `Error`

```badger
struct Error { pub node: Symbol, pub message: String, pub notes: List<String>, pub original: Option<String>, pub cause: Option<system.ProviderError> }
```

A startup or cleanup failure, with cleanup failures attached. When
cleanup fails after the body already failed, `original` keeps the body's
error (it is never silently replaced).

### `InitScope`

```badger
struct InitScope<S> { brand: system.Brand<S>, halts: Cell<List<fn() -> Option<String>>>, tasks: Int, workers: Cell<List<(Int, worker.Shutdown)>>, node: Symbol, stopping: Cell<Bool> }
```

Initialization scope of one node: registers halt callbacks and owns the
node's workers.
A node's initialization scope, for the node's region `S` (elidable in
annotations: `system.InitScope` means `system.InitScope<_>`). Resources
acquired and callbacks registered here live until the node halts.

#### `InitScope.acquire`

```badger
fn acquire<C, O, E>(self: &Self, provider: Provider<C, O, E>, config: C) -> Result<O, E>
```

Acquire a nested resource whose cleanup belongs to this scope.

#### `InitScope.on_halt`

```badger
fn on_halt<E>(self: &Self, f: once fn() -> Result<Unit, E>) -> Unit where E: prelude.Error
```

Register a one-shot, possibly fallible cleanup; halts run in reverse
registration order, after the node's workers have settled.

#### `InitScope.worker`

```badger
fn worker<E, Eff>(self: &Self, factory: fn() -> Result<Unit, E> !Eff, policy: worker.Policy) -> Unit where E: prelude.Error, fn() -> Result<Unit, E> !Eff: Transfer
```

Start a managed worker owned by this node (named after the node),
with a restart policy. Halting the node cancels and settles it before
the node's halt callbacks run; an escalated failure fails the system.

#### `InitScope.worker_with`

```badger
fn worker_with<E, Eff>(self: &Self, name: Symbol, factory: fn() -> Result<Unit, E> !Eff, policy: worker.Policy, shutdown: worker.Shutdown) -> Unit where E: prelude.Error, fn() -> Result<Unit, E> !Eff: Transfer
```

`worker` with an explicit name and shutdown policy.

### `Node`

```badger
struct Node<C, O> { pub index: Int, erased: system.ErasedNode }
```

A typed node handle: `ref(:key)` reads its output through `output`;
`C` is its provider's configuration type.

### `Outputs`

```badger
struct Outputs { slots: Cell<Map<Int, system.Erased>>, partial: Bool }
```

Resolved outputs of started nodes. A selected sub-plan reads the full
output view `partial`ly: unstarted nodes yield placeholders that its
projection never reads.

### `Running`

```badger
pub type Running<S, Os: Row> = {
```

A running system: every node output by its plan key, plus control
operations. Branded with the region of `system.run`'s callback.

### `SystemPlan`

```badger
struct SystemPlan<Os, Cs> { pub nodes: List<system.ErasedNode>, view: fn(system.Outputs) -> {..Os} !{Io, Wait, State}, configs: fn(system.Outputs) -> {..Cs} !{Io, Wait, State} }
```

An inspectable, validated system description whose started nodes'
outputs form the record `Os` and whose providers' configurations form
`Cs` (one field per plan key; `Cs` may be elided in annotations).

#### `SystemPlan.describe`

```badger

```

Inspectable description: key, provider, location, dependencies.

#### `SystemPlan.labels`

```badger
fn labels(self: &Self) -> List<Symbol>
```

Node labels in startup order.

### `provider`

```badger
fn provider<C, O, E>(spec: { name: Symbol, init: fn(InitScope<Unit>, C) -> Result<O, E> }) -> Provider<C, O, E> where E: prelude.Error, E: Unscoped
```

Create a typed provider. Its errors implement `Error` (and, being
errors, carry no resources).

### `replace`

```badger
fn replace<Os: Row, Cs: Row, C, O, E>(plan: SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, key: Symbol, provider: Provider<C, O, E>) -> Result<SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, Error> where E: prelude.Error
```

`system.replace(plan, :key, provider)`: the same plan with one node's
provider replaced (tests). The replacement keeps the node's declared
configuration and output contract, checked statically (the compiler
supplies `pick` and `pick_config`).

### `replace_node`

```badger
fn replace_node<Os: Row, Cs: Row, C, O, E>(plan: SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, key: Symbol, provider: Provider<C, O, E>, pick: fn({ ..Os }) -> O, pick_config: fn({ ..Cs }) -> C) -> Result<SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, Error> where E: prelude.Error
```

### `run`

```badger
fn run<Os: Row, Cs: Row, R, E>(plan: SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, body: for<S: Scope> fn(Running<S, Os>) -> Result<R, E>) -> Result<R, E> !{Io, Wait, State} where E: From<Error>, E: Display
```

Start every node in dependency order, run `body`, then halt in reverse.
If startup fails, already-started nodes halt and their cleanup failures
attach to the original error.

### `select`

```badger
fn select<Os: Row, Cs: Row>(plan: SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, keys: List<Symbol>) -> SystemPlan<Os, Cs>
```

`system.select(plan, [:key, ...])`: the sub-plan that starts only the
selected keys and their dependency closure (in the original order), with
just those keys' outputs. The keys must be a literal list; the compiler
rewrites the call to `select_keys` with a typed projection.

### `select_keys`

```badger
fn select_keys<Os: Row, Cs: Row, Sub: Row>(plan: SystemPlan<Os, Cs>, keys: List<Symbol>, pick: fn({ ..Os }) -> { ..Sub }) -> SystemPlan<Sub, Cs>
```
